hymnal.name: Lodge Hymnal
hymnal.lore: A funeral hymnal, margins crowded with a steady old hand: 'For the risen flesh, FLAME. For the unquiet spirit, COLD IRON. For the beasts that never lived, the craft's own SILVER. For the Warden of the Yard — nothing of this world. Endure him.'

revolver.name: Founder's Revolver
revolver.lore: A lodge-engraved top-break revolver, oiled and loaded. Six shots. The founder believed in being prepared for his own funeral.

sextons-ledger.name: The Sexton's Ledger
sextons-ledger.lore: A burial ledger in a cramped, patient hand. The last page is a compact, witnessed by nine seals: 'The Warden of the Yard shall keep Solomon's Rest from dusk-bell to daybreak, and shall claim of trespassers ONLY THE SUNDERED — the one cut off from the flock. While two of the living stand witness to one another he shall not raise his hand, and at first light he shall go below. So mote it be.' Someone has underlined 'only the sundered' three times.

silver-trowel.name: Ceremonial Silver Trowel
silver-trowel.lore: Lodge silver, engraved: 'TO SPREAD THE CEMENT OF BROTHERLY LOVE.' The working tool of the craft — and, the old stories say, the one metal the beasts that never lived cannot abide.

text.value: The ground softens like a held breath, and cold hands close around every living ankle in the yard. They do not pull. They just hold — and the holding is the worst of it.

value.value: The bronze key grinds through a century of verdigris, and the founders door swings inward.

script.failMessage: The bronze door of the founders mausoleum is locked fast. The keyhole is shaped like a compass rose.

text.value: Marble, regalia, and the founder's long oak case. On the sarcophagus lid, freshly dusted as if tended nightly, someone keeps a ledger squared to the corner — the Sexton still makes his rounds in here.
The east goes gray above the yews. Somewhere below, a spade is shouldered: the compact is spent. Daybreak.

entries.1: The dusk-bell fades. Nine o clock, by the chapel chime, and the last daylight drains out of the sky.
entries.2: Ten o clock. The gravel paths have gone silver and strange, and the rows do not seem to line up the way they did.
entries.3: Eleven. A lantern crosses the yard where no path runs. It pauses whenever one of you stands apart from the others.
entries.4: Midnight. The chime goes on one stroke too long. In the after-ring you hear a spade bite earth, patient as a heartbeat.
entries.5: Two in the morning — the chime skipped one entirely. The Sexton has been seen at the edge of the light, waiting. Never while you stand together. Only ever near whoever is alone.
entries.6: Three. The fog comes up to the knee, and under it the ground feels freshly turned. All of it.
entries.7: False dawn — a lie of gray light. The digging sounds have stopped. That is somehow worse.

text.value: The padlock snaps shut behind you and your friends' laughter fades down the road. The dare is simple: last until daybreak inside Solomon's Rest. Somewhere across the yard, right on cue, a bell you cannot see tolls dusk — and something under the ground hears it too.
Far down the rows a lantern swings — a tall figure with a spade over one shoulder, standing very still among the stones. It watches all of you, counts you, and does not come closer. Not yet.
From the chapel a bell tolls — backward, the strokes swallowing themselves. The stars wheel the wrong way, and the night grows two hours longer.
The cold down here is older than the chapel above it. Lodge chests line the walls, and the dust on the floor shows no footprints at all — nothing walks here. Nothing has to.

value.value: The brass key turns twice. The stair-door swings open onto cellar dark.

script.failMessage: The stair-door to the undercroft is locked — a keyhole of old brass, and the Tyler's post stands between you and whatever opens it.

script.description: A woman in mourning gray beneath the willow, her veil moving in a wind you cannot feel. Her grief is a hundred years old and perfectly patient.

response.value: You should never have come in on a dare, children. But you are in now, and the gates keep till morning. Listen to an old widow: whatever else you do tonight, stay TOGETHER. The Sexton walks.

He dug every grave here, and then his own, and did not stop working. The lodge bound him with a compact: from dusk-bell to daybreak he keeps the yard — but he may take only the sundered, the one cut off from the flock. While another living soul stands beside you, his hand is stayed. He knows it. It is why he will try so hard to get you alone.
Endure to first light, dears. At daybreak he must go below — the compact allows him nothing else — and the lychgate will stand open of itself.

The lesser dead can be put down: flame for the risen flesh, cold iron for the unquiet spirit, the craft's silver for the beasts that never lived. But the Sexton is not a thing you fight. He is a thing you outlast.

The Tyler guards the chapel stair as he guarded the lodge door in life — his key goes below with him, unless someone puts him to rest. And the founder was buried with everything he valued, behind bronze. His wight keeps the bronze key, out among the mausoleums.

cold-hands.name: Cold Hands from Below
cold-hands.text: Fingers close around every living ankle in the yard.

toll-the-black-bell.name: Toll the Black Bell
toll-the-black-bell.text: The chapel bell rings backward, and the night grows two hours longer.

wicked:lights-out.name: Lights Out
wicked:lights-out.text: Every flame in the cemetery gutters and dies.

wicked:ruin.name: Rot and Ruin
wicked:ruin.text: What you carry, the grave-damp claims.

wicked:scatter.name: Scatter the Flock
wicked:scatter.text: The ground opens under every pair of feet at once.

wicked:shadow-step.name: Shadow Step
wicked:shadow-step.text: The Sexton is where the lantern-light is not.
